evidence.text: Can a globally consistent Type IIA intersecting-D6 compactification realize four-form relaxation of strong CP while preserving axion quality, moduli stabilization and small uplift backreaction, with compatible swampland constraints and observable axion parameters?

sources.title: Strong CP Problem in Type IIA Toroidal Orientifold String Theory

evidence.text: F-term conditions W=∂T W=∂S W=∂U W=0 define the Minkowski baseline. Stability and uplift shifts are treated using potential second derivatives and linearized coupled real-modulus/axion extremum equations, with anti-D6 energy represented by a nilpotent-superfield potential.

sources.title: Strong CP Problem in Type IIA Toroidal Orientifold String Theory

evidence.text: Democratic Type IIA formulation, harmonic-form dimensional reduction and equation-of-motion Hodge duality; auxiliary four-forms are integrated out, followed by term matching between the string flux potential and the low-energy QCD four-form description.

destination.title: Stabilized vacua and supersymmetry breaking
destination.question: Under which geometric and correction assumptions can IIB compactifications stabilize moduli in AdS, nearly Minkowski or de Sitter vacua, and what supersymmetry-breaking scales follow?
destination.summary: Compare single-modulus constructions, large-volume mechanisms and purely perturbative alternatives. Vacuum existence, uplift, stability and particle scales are distinct requirements.

targets: Spontaneous supersymmetry breaking and soft scales
Geometric requirements for stabilization and uplift
assumptions: The simplest single-modulus examples have high soft scales; the reported low-gravitino-mass example uses several nonperturbative terms.
The purely perturbative example lacks divisor topologies needed for nonperturbative superpotential contributions.
includes: AdS solutions and proposed uplift prescriptions
Comparisons among KKLT, racetrack, LVS and perturbative LVS
excludes: A universal requirement for nonperturbative superpotentials
Certification of controlled de Sitter vacua from introductory excerpts

sources.title: Physical Vacua in IIB Compactifications with a Single Kaehler Modulus

evidence.text: Can type IIB Calabi–Yau orientifold compactifications with one Kähler modulus produce nearly Minkowski or de Sitter vacua with spontaneous SUSY breaking and TeV-scale superpartners, while avoiding the additional flavor constraints motivating the single-modulus restriction?

sources.title: Seeking de Sitter vacua in the string landscape

evidence.text: Review how type IIB Calabi–Yau orientifolds can stabilise moduli and realise de Sitter vacua, particularly through purely perturbative corrections, and which geometric requirements permit a concrete global embedding.

sources.title: Stabilising all Kähler moduli in perturbative LVS

evidence.text: Can perturbative α′, string-loop and higher-derivative corrections stabilize the overall volume and remaining Kähler size moduli at exponentially large volume, and can additional uplift terms produce de Sitter minima?

sources.title: Physical Vacua in IIB Compactifications with a Single Kaehler Modulus

evidence.text: For simultaneous S,T breaking, expand W around a proposed real vacuum and match Taylor coefficients through third order, which determine the potential Hessian. Numerical work uses Mathematica minimization and STRINGVACUA for simplification, without its algebraic-geometry algorithms.

sources.title: Stabilising all Kähler moduli in perturbative LVS

evidence.text: Use weak-coupling and large-volume expansions, analytic volume extremization and second derivatives, followed by numerical minimization in the three tα directions. Inspect Hessian eigenvalues for selected uplifted examples.

sources.title: Seeking de Sitter vacua in the string landscape

evidence.text: Review logarithmic corrections from an R4-induced localised Einstein–Hilbert vertex exchanging KK gravitons with D7 stacks through two transverse dimensions. The amplitude discussion uses an orbifold limit before its CY interpretation.

sources.title: Physical Vacua in IIB Compactifications with a Single Kaehler Modulus

evidence.text: Large-volume expansion of the scalar potential, axion extremization, and positivity tests for the t–τ Hessian are used analytically. Soft scalar masses are evaluated using supergravity F-terms and matter-field curvature.

sources.title: Stabilising all Kähler moduli in perturbative LVS

evidence.text: Parametrize volume-dependent one-loop effects by f(V), compute the corrected Kähler metric, and invert it through four auxiliary coefficient equations. Derive no-scale-breaking identities and a scalar-potential master formula, then add KK, winding and F⁴ terms.

sources.title: Seeking de Sitter vacua in the string landscape

evidence.text: Organise scalar potentials through master formulae using intersection numbers, Euler characteristic and two-cycle variables; present large-volume expansions, three-field numerical extrema and reported Hessian eigenvalues.

sources.title: Global Orientifolded Quivers with Inflation

evidence.text: Can an orientifolded chiral quiver at a singularity be embedded in a compact type-IIB model satisfying global brane constraints, with stabilized closed-string moduli, a tunable Minkowski/de Sitter vacuum and viable inflation in the same geometry?

sources.title: Aspects of moduli stabilisation in string and M-theory

evidence.text: Can flux compactifications stabilise geometric moduli, and can type IIB conifold transitions dynamically complete rather than trap moduli? The thesis studies the resulting four-dimensional effective theories and their cosmological dynamics.

sources.title: The Standard Model quiver in de Sitter string compactifications

evidence.text: Can an orientifolded D3-brane Standard Model quiver be embedded in a compact type IIB Calabi–Yau with consistent brane charges, moduli stabilisation, supersymmetry breaking and a controlled de Sitter minimum?

sources.title: Systematics of moduli stabilisation in Calabi-Yau flux compactifications

evidence.text: Can leading α′ corrections combined with nonperturbative effects stabilize type IIB compactifications at exponentially large volume without a hierarchically small flux superpotential, and yield stable nonsupersymmetric AdS or uplifted de Sitter vacua? How do the gravitino and string scales depend on flux choices?

sources.title: Moduli Stabilisation and Applications in IIB String Theory

evidence.text: How can IIB compactification moduli be stabilised with controlled corrections, and how can the resulting potentials support supersymmetry breaking, QCD axions and inflation?
